rows.selection_reason: The existing evidence is nonexistent, so the first experiment should establish a baseline by testing a simple RNA-only model with PCA encoding. This clarifies the performance of a basic unimodal approach, isolating the effect of RNA data representation. Testing this configuration first provides a reference point to compare against more complex multimodal setups in subsequent experiments.

The existing evidence shows that RNA-only singleprofile with PCA achieves 0.4849 accuracy. This experiment tests multiprofile with avgpool aggregation (vs. no aggregation in config_001), isolating the effect of profile setting and aggregation. It balances exploration (testing multiprofile) with exploitation (maintaining RNA-only and PCA encoder), and addresses a key design choice with minimal changes.

Existing evidence shows multiprofile RNA-only models (config_002) outperform singleprofile (config_001). This experiment tests transformer aggregation (vs config_002's avgpool) in the same multiprofile RNA-only setting, isolating the effect of aggregation method. It balances exploration of critical design choices while building on the promising multiprofile direction.

Existing evidence shows that RNA-only multiprofile models with avgpool aggregation (config_002, 0.591 accuracy) outperform singleprofile and other encoders. This experiment tests replacing pca_n2000 with scvi_n200 (a more expressive encoder) in the same setup to isolate the impact of RNA encoder choice. It balances exploitation of the multiprofile/avgpool pattern with exploration of encoder improvements, which could yield higher accuracy without overcomplicating the model.

The existing evidence shows that using scvi_n200 RNA encoder with multiprofile and avgpool aggregation (config_005) achieves the highest accuracy so far (0.6501). This experiment tests whether changing the aggregation method to transformer (while keeping rna_only, multiprofile, and scvi_n200) could further improve performance. This clarifies the impact of aggregation strategy on model performance, balancing exploitation of the current top configuration with exploration of key design choices.

Existing evidence shows RNA-only models with scvi_n200 encoder and transformer aggregation (config_006) achieve the highest accuracy so far (0.653). This experiment tests a multimodal model combining scvi_n200 RNA encoder with resnet50 image encoder, using transformer aggregation and concat fusion. It isolates the effect of adding image data to the best RNA-only configuration, balancing exploration of multimodal benefits against exploitation of the current RNA-only success.

The existing evidence shows that multimodal models with scvi_n200 and resnet50 (e.g., config_032) achieve the highest accuracy so far (0.6878). This experiment tests whether switching from concat to weighted fusion (a critical design choice) further improves performance. It isolates the effect of fusion strategy while maintaining the proven combination of scvi_n200, resnet50, and transformer aggregation, balancing exploitation of current strengths with exploration of key architectural variations.

The existing evidence shows that multimodal models with scvi_n200 RNA encoder, transformer aggregation, and weighted fusion (config_033) achieve the highest accuracy so far (0.713). This experiment tests whether replacing resnet50 with a more advanced image encoder (imagenet_vit_l) further improves performance while keeping RNA encoder, aggregation, and fusion methods consistent. This isolates the impact of the image encoder, a critical design choice, and leverages the strong prior evidence to explore a promising direction without changing multiple variables.

The existing evidence shows that multimodal models with scvi_n200 and imagenet_vit_l (config_039) achieve the highest accuracy so far (0.725). This experiment tests whether switching the RNA encoder to scgpt (a more advanced model) while retaining the top-performing image encoder and fusion strategy could further improve accuracy. It directly addresses the uncertainty around the RNA encoder's impact on multimodal performance, leveraging the remaining budget to explore a high-impact design choice.

The existing evidence shows that multimodal models with scvi_n200 RNA encoder, imagenet_vit_l image encoder, transformer aggregation, and weighted fusion (config_039) achieve the highest accuracy so far (0.724989). This experiment tests a similar configuration but with concat fusion instead of weighted fusion, isolating the effect of fusion type. It is the best use of the final budget to explore whether a simpler fusion method could match or exceed the current best, while avoiding redundant changes to other components.
